answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a bond-and-attestation registry. Every agent locks its own stake and weaves a thread of vouchers from other bonded agents, each voucher bound to a unique, one-time pulse that cannot be transferred or replayed. To mint k fake identities an attacker must post k separate bonds and buy k independent vouchers; if any clone is caught, its bond is slashed. The cost therefore grows with each spurious node, while honest participants, scattered even across the tundra of a thin market, keep real collateral at risk, making mass registration uneconomical.
